- **self**: Salesforce CDC versus custom Platform Events for Case alerting (12/2)

## Definitions

- [statement] Automatic CDC generation is not an absolute no-loss guarantee: Salesforce documents rare cases where change messages are not persisted, delivered, or recoverable. Avoid presenting CDC-based Case alerts as transactionally guaranteed delivery. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/change-data-capture/guide/cdc-when-to-use.html · keywords: Salesforce CDC versus custom Platform Events for Case alerting

## How it works

- [statement] Custom alert publishing must cover every relevant write path. SFHooks specifically warns that data-loader changes, API edits, and packages can be missed when those paths forget to publish. (low confidence) — https://sfhooks.com/vs/platform-events · keywords: Salesforce CDC versus custom Platform Events for Case alerting
- [statement] CDC stream filtering reduces event delivery allocation usage because usage counts events delivered after filtering. This scopes the argument that every subscriber must receive every record change. (high confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/change-data-capture/guide/cdc-filter-event-allocations.html · keywords: Salesforce CDC versus custom Platform Events for Case alerting · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/change-data-capture/guide/cdc-allocations.html
- [statement] Custom Platform Events let an application define the payload schema and publish business signals from Apex, Flow, or an API. Defining the event alone does not publish those signals. (high confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/platform-events/guide/platform-events-define.html · keywords: Salesforce CDC versus custom Platform Events for Case alerting · also: https://sfhooks.com/vs/platform-events
- [statement] For custom Platform Events published within Salesforce transactions, Publish After Commit publishes only after a successful commit and suppresses publication when the transaction fails. The setting does not apply to messages published with Pub/Sub API. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/platform-events/guide/platform-events-define-ui.html · keywords: Salesforce CDC versus custom Platform Events for Case alerting

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Current Salesforce allocation documentation states that CDC has no publishing limit because Salesforce publishes changes automatically. Do not infer a CDC publishing quota from the older design blog’s general discussion of publish and subscribe limits. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/change-data-capture/guide/cdc-allocations.html · keywords: Salesforce CDC versus custom Platform Events for Case alerting · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/blogs/2022/10/design-considerations-for-change-data-capture-and-platform-events

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] A custom Platform Event lets the alert producer define the payload with custom fields, making it suitable for a named Case business alert rather than a raw record delta; this is an architectural inference from the documented event model. (high confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/platform-events/guide/platform-events-define.html · keywords: Salesforce CDC versus custom Platform Events for Case alerting · also: https://sfhooks.com/vs/platform-events
- [statement] CDC automatically provides record-change notifications rather than requiring a custom event definition and explicit publisher for every notification. Salesforce documents notifications for creates, updates, deletes, and undeletes. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/blogs/2022/10/design-considerations-for-change-data-capture-and-platform-events · keywords: Salesforce CDC versus custom Platform Events for Case alerting

## Facts and statements

- [statement] CDC automatically emits record-change notifications for enabled objects; custom Platform Events require an explicit publisher and a custom event definition. For Case alerting, this is the choice between reacting to data changes and publishing a deliberate business signal. (high confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/blogs/2022/10/design-considerations-for-change-data-capture-and-platform-events · keywords: Salesforce CDC versus custom Platform Events for Case alerting · also: https://sfhooks.com/vs/platform-events
- [statement] Pub/Sub API supports both high-volume custom Platform Events and CDC events, so choosing between these event models does not require a different subscription API. (high confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/supported-event-types.html · keywords: Salesforce CDC versus custom Platform Events for Case alerting · also: https://sfhooks.com/vs/platform-events
- [statement] High-volume Platform Events and CDC share the event delivery allocation, and each subscribed client adds to usage; switching event type alone does not create an independent delivery budget. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/change-data-capture/guide/cdc-allocations.html · keywords: Salesforce CDC versus custom Platform Events for Case alerting
- [statement] For a custom Case alert whose consumer needs committed transaction data, configure Publish After Commit. Publish Immediately can emit despite a failed transaction or before its data commits. The event definition’s publish behavior does not apply to messages published with Pub/Sub API. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/platform-events/guide/platform-events-define-ui.html · keywords: Salesforce CDC versus custom Platform Events for Case alerting

## Research summary — Salesforce CDC versus custom Platform Events for Case alerting

CDC automatically reports record changes on enabled objects. Custom Platform Events carry a producer-defined business signal and payload. For Case alerting, CDC avoids custom publishing coverage, while custom events allow a deliberate alert contract. Filtered CDC channels can reduce delivery volume, so selectivity alone does not mandate custom events. Both event types use Pub/Sub API and share the delivery allocation. Custom-event publish timing must match the consumer’s need for committed data. CDC is asynchronous and is not an absolute no-loss guarantee. These are design implications of the documented event models; this probe does not prescribe Case transition rules.
